title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: Show me a manufacturer's inventory days and receivable days, and I will tell you who holds the bargaining power in the supply chain.
epigraph.author: Working Capital Forensics

web_blocks.html: BEML's go-to-market model is direct institutional bidding paired with a nationwide aftermarket service network, rather than dealer-led retail distribution. Over 75% of revenue is won through competitive tenders against domestic and global OEMs. To service heavy fleets deployed in remote coalfields, border areas.Urban metro depots, BEML operates 12 regional offices, 16 district offices.Temporary on-site activity centres, coordinated by a central Contract Management Cell at KGF. In 2026, management began commissioning a dedicated hub-and-spoke spares and assembly centre on 80 acres in Mungeli near Bilaspur. Chhattisgarh—cutting response times to Coal India subsidiaries from several days to 24–48 hours.

On the manufacturing side, BEML acts primarily as a system integrator with high engineering value-add, outsourcing standardized fabrications and components to domestic MSMEs while retaining critical machining, chassis welding, powertrain integration, and testing in-house. To break capacity bottlenecks in rolling stock—where legacy Bengaluru lines produced roughly 250 coaches per year—BEML invested ₹250 crore in the new 'Aditya' high-speed rail complex in Bengaluru (operational in 2026) and broke ground on the ₹900 crore Phase-1 'BRAHMA' greenfield rolling-stock plant in Bhopal, which will add 700–800 rail cars per year once commissioned.

web_blocks.takeaway: In FY26, every ₹100 of BEML revenue generated ₹6.87 of operating EBITDA, ₹3.24 of net profit, ₹2.71 of operating cash flow, and -₹4.78 of Free Cash Flow after ₹7.49 of expansion capex.

web_blocks.html: The ₹100 unit-economics waterfall exposes BEML's central structural tension. First, employee expenses and fixed plant overheads absorb roughly 32% of sales in a normal year, creating sharp operating leverage. When revenue drops below ₹700 crore in Q1 (as in Jun 2024 and Jun 2025), operating profit turns negative. When Q4 dispatches hit ₹1,653–₹1,794 crore, operating margins expand to 15%–26%. Second, raw material costs jumped to 61% of revenue in FY26 and Q2 FY27 due to imported metro/rail subsystems, prototype development costs on Vande Bharat Sleeper. Foreign-exchange timing mismatches. Third, even when BEML earns accounting profit, working capital absorbs most of it. In FY26, only ₹2.71 out of every ₹100 of sales reached operating cash flow. That forces the company to borrow to fund its ₹326 crore capex.

web_blocks.title: Why Margin & Working Capital Volatility Persist
paragraphs: Customer-side bottlenecks frequently trap BEML's finished inventory on the balance sheet. In FY25, CARE Ratings noted that ~₹800 crore of Mumbai Metro rolling-stock deliveries were delayed because the Mandale Metro depot lacked storage readiness. Because revenue cannot be booked until customer inspection and site handover, BEML carries raw materials, work-in-progress.Finished trainsets for 394–462 days.

Meanwhile, on the aftermarket side, spares and Maintenance & Repair Contracts (MARC) carry substantially higher gross margins than base equipment—CMD Shantanu Roy explicitly ranked spares/sustenance #1 and exports #2 in margin hierarchy during the August 2026 concall. Until spares and high-margin defence systems scale past 30%–35% of revenue and quarterly dispatches smooth out from the historical 10/20/30/40 Q1–Q4 skew, unit economics will remain vulnerable to input-cost spikes.

book_paragraphs: To understand how BEML makes money—and why its profits bounce around so violently—you and I need to trace its supply chain and follow ₹100 of revenue down to free cash flow. Unlike a consumer brand or a private construction equipment dealer, BEML does not sell through third-party showrooms. Over three-quarters of its business comes from direct competitive tenders floated by Coal India, the Ministry of Defence, Indian Railways, and city metro corporations.

Let us walk through how a rupee of revenue actually travels through BEML's factories and turns—or fails to turn—into free cash flow. Unlike consumer goods companies that sell through distributors on cash-and-carry terms, BEML sells almost entirely through direct government-to-government tenders and L1 (lowest-bidder) public auctions. For Mining and Construction, BEML operates a nationwide Maintenance and Repair Contract (MARC) network with regional depots in Bilaspur, Nagpur, and Singrauli, stationing engineers directly at Coal India pitheads so downtime on a 150-ton dumper stays under 12 hours.

For Rail and Metro and Defence, the go-to-market cycle is a marathon of technical pre-qualification, prototype inspection by RDSO or military quality-assurance wings, and milestone-based invoicing. Because state-owned buyers release 10% to 20% of contract value only after final commissioning and warranty sign-offs, BEML's trade receivables ballooned to 191 days in recent periods, stretching its cash conversion cycle to roughly 421 days. When you look at the audited FY26 ₹100 revenue waterfall, ₹62 goes to raw materials and bought-out components, ₹21 goes to a sticky unionized employee base, and only ₹7 survives as operating profit before depreciation, interest, and taxes.

Once you subtract ₹208 crore of negative free cash flow in FY26—driven by ₹260 crore+ of modernization capex and heavy working-capital absorption—you see the core unit-economics tension. BEML is not a capital-light compounding machine; it is a heavy engineering integrator that must continually fund inventory and state-buyer receivables upfront just to grow its top line.

book_subsections.title: Direct Institutional Distribution and the Bilaspur Hub
paragraphs: Once heavy machines leave BEML's plants, the company supports them directly through 12 regional offices, 16 district offices, and on-site engineering teams stationed right inside coal mines and army workshops, all coordinated by a central Contract Management Cell at Kolar Gold Fields. In 2026, BEML moved closer to its largest mining buyers by developing an 80-acre hub-and-spoke spares and assembly centre near Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, cutting response times to Coal India pitheads from several days to 24–48 hours.

That direct model gives BEML a sticky aftermarket moat. When a Coal India subsidiary signs a Guaranteed Availability or Maintenance and Repair Contract, BEML's technicians keep the 100-tonne dumpers running and supply every replacement hydraulic cylinder, axle, and filter. As Chairman Shantanu Roy confirmed on the Q1 FY27 call, spares and sustenance are the single highest-margin business inside BEML, followed closely by exports.

book_subsections.title: Inside the FY26 ₹100 Waterfall
paragraphs: Now look at the ₹100 waterfall for FY26, when audited revenue hit ₹4,351 crore. Out of every ₹100 billed, roughly ₹61 went straight out the door for steel, imported metro propulsion components, and sub-assemblies. Another ₹20.50 paid for BEML's permanent PSU engineering and shop-floor workforce, and nearly ₹12 covered power, freight, R&D, and overhead. That left just ₹6.87 of operating EBITDA—down sharply from ₹12.60 in FY25—because prototype costs, one-off adjustments, and higher material costs squeezed the middle of the income statement.

After deducting ₹1.91 for depreciation, ₹1.03 for interest, and ₹1.36 for taxes (offset slightly by ₹0.67 of other income), reported net profit was ₹3.24 per ₹100 of sales. Worse, because trade receivables stretched to 191 days and inventory sat at 394 days, working capital ate up most of that profit, leaving only ₹2.71 of cash flow from operations. With BEML spending ₹7.49 per ₹100 of sales on capital expenditure for its new Aditya high-speed rail facility and Bhopal prep, Free Cash Flow was negative ₹4.78 per ₹100 of revenue.

book_subsections.title: Why Growth Consumes Cash Before It Pays Cash
paragraphs: That negative ₹4.78 free cash flow per ₹100 of sales explains why BEML's borrowings tripled between March 2024 and September 2026: growth in heavy rolling stock consumes cash before it generates cash. When Mumbai Metro's Mandale depot was not ready to receive finished trainsets in FY25, ~₹800 crore of revenue sat frozen on BEML's shop floor.

Until spares and high-margin defence systems scale past 30%–35% of total revenue and quarterly dispatches smooth out from their historical 10/20/30/40 March-quarter skew, unit economics will remain sensitive to input-cost swings and customer handover schedules. Next, let us examine who BEML competes against in these tenders and whether its moat is widening or narrowing.

book_subsections.title: The Working Capital Trap: Tracing Cash from Tender to Bank Account
paragraphs: Imagine you run a factory that builds a ₹100 crore batch of metro coaches for a state urban rail corporation. Before you even cut the first sheet of stainless steel, you must procure bogies, braking systems, traction motors, and interior fittings from domestic and European suppliers who demand payment within 30 to 60 days. Your engineers and shop-floor technicians draw salaries every single month for the next year while the coaches are assembled and tested.

When the trainset finally rolls onto the test track, the state buyer pays 70% to 80% on delivery milestones, but holds back 10% to 20% as retention money until trial runs and warranty periods conclude—often 12 to 24 months later. That timing mismatch is why BEML's debtor days sit at 191 days and its cash conversion cycle stretches past 420 days. Every time BEML accelerates top-line execution in Rail and Metro, it must fund that working-capital bridge out of internal cash or short-term borrowings, explaining why free cash flow stayed negative in FY25 and FY26.

book_subsections.title: Why Unionized Fixed Costs Amplify Quarterly Seasonality
paragraphs: In most heavy-engineering PSUs, employee benefit expenses behave like a fixed bond coupon—roughly ₹900 crore a year at BEML regardless of whether Q1 factory output is ₹634 crore or Q4 output is ₹1,794 crore. When Q1 dispatches slow down due to government budget approvals or monsoon mining halts, those fixed payrolls push Q1 operating profit into the red, as we saw in both Jun 2024 (-₹50 crore) and Jun 2025 (-₹49 crore).

Then, every March, engineers and project managers rush to clear RDSO and defence inspections before the fiscal year closes, producing a massive Q4 revenue spike. Understanding that structural rhythm prevents you from overreacting to a weak June quarter—and prevents you from annualizing a peak March quarter.

book_subsections.title: Capex Intensity and the Bhopal Greenfield Expansion
paragraphs: Unlike asset-light software or specialty-chemical leaders that can scale volume with minimal incremental plant investment, BEML must continually invest in heavy fabrication bays, robotic welding lines, and test tracks. Recent annual capex at ₹326 crore—including the greenfield rail manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh—absorbs more than 100% of operating cash flow in lean margin years. Until that new capacity reaches high utilization and generates positive free cash flow after maintenance and growth capex, shareholders are funding expansion rather than harvesting cash.

book_subsections.title: Why Inventory and Retention Money Matter More Than Headline Sales
paragraphs: Whenever you audit a heavy-engineering contractor, read the balance sheet before the income statement. Revenue can be booked upon milestone dispatch, but real economic value only arrives when retention money clears warranty inspections and lands in the company bank account as unrestricted operating cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Why Supplier Credit Cannot Offset Slow State Collections
paragraphs: Even when BEML negotiates standard credit terms with domestic and European component vendors, 45-to-60-day payable cycles cannot match 191-day customer collection cycles. That structural working-capital gap means every ₹100 crore of incremental metro or defence revenue requires substantial upfront cash investment before final milestone payments arrive.
